foot: Free forever: no subscriptions, ads or data collection.
pain.1.s: Three or four CAD programs open every day, each with its own idea of the mouse. By lunch your hand spins the part the wrong way.
pain.1.x: Ready presets like Inventor, KOMPAS-3D, SolidWorks and Blender — or your own: any button with Shift, Ctrl or Alt. A separate tab for the touchpad.
pain.2.t: A thread that exists only in the picture
pain.2.s: You cut a thread, send it to the slicer — and get a smooth cylinder. The thread was just a texture on the face.
pain.2.x: Click a 6.8 mm hole and BreezeCAD knows it is M8. Real ISO 60° geometry goes straight to STL and 3MF.
pain.3.t: The window hides what you wanted to click
pain.3.s: Start a measurement and the result window lands right on the edge you need to pick.
pain.3.x: Results and parameters live in the left panel. Each picked item has its own field with a cross; a missed click resets nothing.
pain.4.s: Nobody invented this reflex, it was trained into us — at the cost of hours lost with a crashed window.
pain.4.x: Autosave every 2, 5 or 10 minutes, even mid-sketch. After a crash one button brings you back where you stopped.
